slot.brief: Given a diagram showing a compass/inclination at a place, use the dip angle relation to find the horizontal or vertical component of Earth's field.

stem: As shown in the figure, the Earth's magnetic field at a location has magnitude $10\times10^{-5}$ T and dip angle $60^\circ$. What is its horizontal component?

verdicts.working: Using the figure, the dip angle is measured from the horizontal, so the horizontal component is B cos 60° = 5×10⁻⁵ T.

working:
$B_H=B\cos\delta$
$B_H=(10\times10^{-5})\cos60^\circ=5\times10^{-5}\ \text{T}$

Independent check: Using the figure, the dip angle is measured from the horizontal, so the horizontal component is B cos 60° = 5×10⁻⁵ T.

draft.stem: As shown in the figure, the Earth's magnetic field at a location has magnitude $10\times10^{-5}$ T and dip angle $60^\circ$. What is its horizontal component?

figure.description: Draw perpendicular horizontal and vertical axes meeting at a point O. From O, draw an arrow representing the Earth's magnetic field vector B, directed upwards and to the right, making an angle of 60° with the positive horizontal axis. Label the vector B = 10 × 10⁻⁵ T and mark the 60° angle between B and the horizontal axis. Label the horizontal axis 'Horizontal plane' and the vertical axis 'Vertical'. Do not draw component arrows.

draft.distractor_notes: B: uses $B\sin60^\circ$, giving the vertical component. C: reports the total field without resolving it. D: uses $B\tan60^\circ$ instead of projecting the field.
